newsitem.title: UK: UK seeks news of Britons said seized in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: UK seeks news of Britons said seized in Chechnya.

text.p: Britain said on Saturday it was urgently seeking information on the whereabouts of two British aid workers reported kidnapped in Russia's breakaway Chechnya region.
Interfax news agency said the two, a married couple working for the Grozny-based Centre for Peace and Development, were seized at gunpoint on Thursday night.

"Our embassy in Moscow is urgently seeking to obtain information about their whereabouts, including through the OSCE (Organisation for Security and Co-Operation in Europe)," a British Foreign Office spokesman said.

"We have been in contact with a representative of the Centre for Peacekeeping and Community Development, who confirmed that two Britons have been working for them in Grozny since early April," the spokesman added.
He said British ministers were concerned for the welfare of the two and were following developments closely.

The Centre for Peace and Development is a Russian non-governmental agency which sometimes employs foreigners to work with some of the children caught up in 21 months of fighting between Chechen separatists and Russian troops.

Gangs have regularly taken hostages in Chechnya and demanded ransom since fighting with Russia ended last August. Interfax said several dozen people were currently being held, including five Russian television journalists.
Interfax quoted an official from Chechnya's Interior Ministry as saying three people had been arrested on Saturday morning in connection with the kidnappings.

Two were the couple's bodyguards, who allegedly did nothing to stop them being taken and did not inform police and the third was the deputy director for the Centre for Child Rehabilitation, the official said.
Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov has issued a decree saying hostage-takers would face the death penalty and their accomplices would get 15 years in jail.
